secrets.title: Secrets & Rotation Management
secrets.subtitle: Background scheduler worker automatically rotates cryptographic keys, synchronizes multi-node local caches via Redis Invalidation Bus, and secures key materials.
secrets.callout_desc: Aurora's secret rotation mechanism is designed according to Zero-Downtime HA standards. While a new Primary Version is promoted to serve new signature generation, the retired Candidate versions remain operational during the Grace Period to successfully validate old tokens, eliminating user disruption.
secrets.sec1_desc: All keys used for encryption or signature generation are centrally registered and managed in the core_secret_families structural table. Below are the real-time operational parameters from the Database Source of Truth:
secrets.sec2_desc: The system ensures data consistency and persistence through strict relationship constraints between core_secret_families and core_secret_versions. Key materials are never stored in plaintext; all payloads are symmetrically encrypted before writing to disk.
secrets.sec2_callout_desc: All key materials must be stored inside secret_ciphertext (encrypted via KMS). The secret_fingerprint contains a non-reversible cryptographic hash to facilitate collision checking without exposing the key material.
secrets.sec2_table_title: Database Lifecycle and Grace Period Specifications
secrets.sec2_sub1_desc: Each family is strictly constrained to have at most one active primary signing key version at a time to prevent signature ambiguity and collision:
secrets.sec2_sub2_title: 2. AES-256-GCM symmetric encryption via Runtime Master Key
secrets.sec2_sub2_desc: Guarantees absolute key material security at-rest. All secret payloads are symmetrically encrypted using AES-256-GCM using the 32-byte SECURITY_RUNTIME_MASTER_KEY provided via environment variables at bootstrap:
secrets.sec2_sub3_desc1: To optimize query performance and prevent data footprint bloating of sensitive key materials, Aurora enforces a strict Version-Set Invariant: each Secret Family maintains at most 2 active versions inside the database (1 Primary Active for signing, and at most 1 Retired Candidate for verification).
secrets.sec2_sub3_desc2: When a Primary Version expires or rotates, it is not deleted immediately. It is demoted to RETIRED and persists for exactly one TTL cycle (Grace Period) to ensure outstanding tokens verify successfully. At the next rotation cycle, the oldest RETIRED version is physically pruned (DELETE) to make space for the newcomer, ensuring a strict size boundary of 2.
secrets.sec3_desc: A background Goroutine worker executes a periodic ticker to evaluate RotateAt. Upon expiration, the worker secures an atomic lock, writes the new version to the database, and publishes a cache invalidation signal to all API nodes via the Redis Invalidation Bus.
